ai.subject: Physiology
ai.summary: LH is a pituitary gonadotropin that triggers ovulation in women and stimulates testosterone production in men. It acts via cAMP/PKA to activate steroidogenic enzymes. Clinical problems arise when LH is too low or too high, affecting fertility and endocrine balance.

sections.p: LH is a glycoprotein hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary. It binds LH receptors on ovarian granulosa cells and Leydig cells, initiating steroidogenesis and ovulation or testosterone synthesis.
b: Produced in response to GnRH pulses

sections.p: LH binds its receptor, activating adenylate cyclase and raising cAMP. This activates PKA, which phosphorylates StAR and P450scc, enabling cholesterol transport into mitochondria and conversion to pregnenolone, the steroid precursor.

t.b: High LH + low estrogen = primary ovarian failure; Low LH + low testosterone = secondary hypogonadism

sections.p: GnRH pulses from hypothalamus control LH secretion. The preovulatory LH surge is a sharp peak at day 14 of the cycle, driven by rising estradiol. In men, LH is regulated by testosterone negative feedback.
b: GnRH pulse frequency determines LH vs FSH

t.b: Low pulse frequency = low LH; high frequency = high LH

sections.p: Disorders include primary ovarian insufficiency, Klinefelter syndrome, pituitary adenomas, and chronic infections like HIV that damage gonads. Low LH leads to infertility; high LH can cause ovarian hyperstimulation.

t.b: High estradiol with low LH suggests pituitary dysfunction
Low testosterone with high LH indicates primary testicular failure

sections.p: LH measurement guides fertility treatment, evaluates endocrine disorders, and monitors response to gonadotropin therapy. In low-resource settings, clinical signs often guide management when labs are scarce.

t.b: Early follicle growth without LH surge suggests pituitary dysfunction

sections.p: Remember the LH surge triggers ovulation; LH stimulates Leydig cells for testosterone. In hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, both LH and gonadal hormones are low. In primary gonadal failure, LH is high.

faq.a: A rise in estradiol from the dominant follicle feeds back to the hypothalamus, increasing GnRH pulse frequency and triggering a massive LH release.

faq.q: Can LH be high in men?
faq.a: Yes, high LH with low testosterone indicates primary testicular failure; high LH with normal testosterone suggests pituitary resistance.

faq.q: Why is LH important in IVF?
faq.a: Controlled LH levels ensure proper follicle maturation and prevent ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.
